headline: Very Strong El Nino -- RONI +1.97 degC (ASO 2026; legacy ONI +2.46), power index 84/100 (Very High), intensifying rapidly.
episode_status: Established El Nino episode: 5 consecutive seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC (NOAA requires 5).

mjo.note: CPC's newest pentad is 13 days old (25 Oct), too old to say where the active phase is now.

notes: 4 candidate analogs were dropped for being too dissimilar to the current trajectory.

alerts.title: Formal El Nino episode criteria met
alerts.detail: 5 consecutive overlapping seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC, from AMJ 2026. NOAA's five-season rule is satisfied.

alerts.title: Projected to peak in very strong territory
alerts.detail: Ensemble peak +2.28 degC at NDJ 2026, 94% probability of exceeding +2.0 degC.

alerts.title: RONI at or above +2.0 degC - Very strong El Nino
alerts.detail: ASO 2026 RONI is +1.97 degC, which CPC prints as +2.0: Very Strong El Nino conditions this season. An event's category is set by its peak, which is still ahead of it while it is building.

alerts.title: Heat content still rising during an active event
alerts.detail: WWV is +0.052 x10^14 m3 per month and still climbing while the surface anomaly is already large. Events normally begin discharging by this stage; continued recharge means the event has not yet spent its fuel.

alerts.title: Cempaka: rapid intensification, +30 kt in 24 h
alerts.detail: NHC calls 30 kt in 24 hours rapid intensification; this is 30, through 2026-11-07 12Z. Forecast intensity error is at its largest exactly here, so treat the official intensity forecast as a floor rather than a centre.

alerts.title: Third-warmest ASO or better
alerts.detail: Rank 2 of 77 for this calendar season on RONI.

alerts.title: Ocean and atmosphere are coupled
alerts.detail: Composite atmospheric index +1.83 sigma, with 90% of indicators in agreement.

alerts.title: Warm water volume in the top five on record
alerts.detail: Rank 3 of 561 months at +3.16 x10^14 m3.

alerts.title: Still intensifying
alerts.detail: RONI rose +0.28 degC from the previous season (intensifying rapidly).

alerts.title: Invest 94S: high potential for a tropical cyclone within 24 h
alerts.detail: JTWC's advisory of 7 Nov 2026 06:30 UTC places it near 13.6S 54.3E and rates the potential for a significant tropical cyclone within 24 hours high. A tropical cyclone formation alert is in effect until 2026-11-08 06:30 UTC: moving west-southwest at 4 kt, winds 25 to 30 kt, pressure near 1000 mb.

alerts.title: East and central Pacific: 2.6x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 356 units of accumulated cyclone energy against 137 for a normal season by 7 November. 25 named storms, 13 hurricanes, 11 major.

alerts.title: Repeated westerly wind forcing over the warm pool
alerts.detail: 6 months in the last year averaged strongly westerly at 850 hPa in the western Pacific, which is how downwelling Kelvin waves get launched.

alerts.title: Legacy ONI and official RONI diverging
alerts.detail: ONI +2.46 against RONI +1.97, a gap of +0.49 degC. That much of the raw anomaly is the whole tropical ocean running warm rather than the Pacific, which is why CPC has classified on RONI since February 2026.

alerts.title: Atlantic: 0.17x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 20 units against 118 normal by 7 November. A suppressed basin is the expected signature of El Nino in the Atlantic, and it is not a reason to relax: 1992 was a quiet season and it produced Andrew.

alerts.title: Westerly wind event under way: central region, 155E-180, 5S-5N
alerts.detail: 8 days above +2 m/s since 2026-10-28 18Z in CCMP's near-real-time winds to 2026-11-05, peaking at +5.0 m/s on 2026-10-31. Equatorial westerly anomalies force downwelling Kelvin waves east.

alerts.title: Westerly wind event under way: east region, 180-150W, 5S-5N
alerts.detail: 35.5 days above +2 m/s since 2026-10-01 06Z in CCMP's near-real-time winds to 2026-11-05, peaking at +10.1 m/s on 2026-10-12; longer than any of the 351 events in Harrison and Vecchi's 1986-1995 list (at most 32.5 days): a sustained westerly anomaly more than a burst. Equatorial westerly anomalies force downwelling Kelvin waves east.

verdict.name: Atlantic
verdict.note: Reinforced by the east-Pacific flavour of this event.

outlook.label: Eastern East Pacific
outlook.text: 1. Eastern East Pacific: A broad area of low pressure located offshore of Central America continues to produce a large area of showers and thunderstorms. Some development is possible over the next day or two, but unfavorable environmental conditions should end formation chances early next week. Regardless of development, this system is expected to bring areas of heavy rain to portions of Central America through the weekend while it drifts northward. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

outlook.label: Western and Central Atlantic (AL94)
outlook.text: 1. Western and Central Atlantic (AL94): A non-tropical low pressure area located several hundred miles south-southeast of Bermuda is producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. The low could still acquire some subtropical characteristics through tonight before upper-level winds increase on Sunday. The low is forecast to move generally eastward over the western and central subtropical Atlantic during the next couple of days and become absorbed by a new non-tropical low pressure system to its east early next week. Regardless, gale-force winds are likely over parts of the central subtropical Atlantic through the weekend. For more information, including Gale Warnings, see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

outlook.label: Invest 94S
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 94S) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 13.6S 55.4E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 13.6S 54.3E, APPROXIMATELY 392 NM NORTHEAST OF TOAMASINA, MADAGASCAR. ANIMATED MULTISPECTRAL SATELLITE IMAGERY (MSI) AND A 070331Z 91 GHZ MICROWAVE IMAGE DEPICT A CONSOLIDATING LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC), WITH DEVELOPING CENTRAL CONVECTION. ELEVATED WINDS ALONG THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY INDICATE A MORE FAVORABLE CHANCE OF DEVELOPMENT AS SEEN IN A 070435Z METOP-B ASCAT PASS. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS DEPICTS A MARGINALLY FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT WITH WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES OF 29-30C, LOW TO MODERATE VERTICAL WIND SHEAR OF 15-20 KTS, AND GOOD POLEWARD OUTFLOW ALOFT. GLOBAL ENSEMBLE MODELS ARE IN AGREEANCE WITH 94S TRANSITING SLOWLY WESTWARD. GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC MODELS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF ECMWF ARE REMAINING CONSERVATIVE WITH MINIMAL DEVELOPMENT BEFORE MAKING LANDFALL OVER NORTHERN MADAGASCAR. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 25 TO 30 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1000 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS IS UPGRADED TO HIGH. SEE REF A (WTXS21 PGTW 070630) FOR FURTHER DETAILS.

stormfury.verdict: 2 of 2 live storms fail STORMFURY's own criteria. Every one of them fails on supercooled water, which is the criterion no hurricane has ever passed and the reason the programme ended.
reasons: TRIGGER: the seeding agent needs supercooled liquid water and hurricane eyewalls are already glaciated at seeding altitude. Nothing to freeze, so the mechanism never starts. Willoughby et al., Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc., 1985.

MAGNITUDE: across 37 natural eyewall expansions in 13 hurricanes this season, conserving angular momentum predicted a mean 28.0% wind drop and the storms actually gave up 4.3%, overstating it 6.5-fold. A hurricane is fed high-momentum air continuously, so a closed-system argument is an upper bound, not a forecast. STORMFURY's predicted effect came from that same calculation.

DETECTION: 25 of 300 unseeded hurricane intervals this season weakened by at least the 31% STORMFURY claimed for Debbie, and 56 moved that far in one direction or the other. An effect that size is indistinguishable from what hurricanes do untouched, which is what closed the programme.

programme.agencies: US Weather Bureau / NOAA with the US Navy

seeded_storms.name: Esther
seeded_storms.outcome: Flown before STORMFURY formally existed, as the proof of concept that got the programme funded.

seeded_storms.name: Beulah
seeded_storms.claimed: eyewall dissipated and reformed further out
seeded_storms.outcome: The first run missed the target area entirely. The second produced the reformation the hypothesis predicted, which is also what an unseeded eyewall replacement looks like.

seeded_storms.name: Debbie
seeded_storms.outcome: The showcase: five seedings on each of two days. These are the numbers the programme is remembered for, and the ones the natural replacement cycle later explained without any silver iodide.

seeded_storms.name: Ginger
seeded_storms.outcome: A large, diffuse storm with no coherent eyewall to move. It was seeded because it was what was available, which is itself a statement about how rarely the criteria above are met.

criteria.name: Supercooled water to seed

Warm-rain coalescence removes liquid water below the freezing level efficiently enough that little survives to be supercooled, leaving the seeding agent with nearly nothing to act on. The trigger is absent. The mechanism cannot start.

cpc_discussion.synopsis: El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
cpc_discussion.body:
El Nino strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Nino indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Nino-3.4, +3.0°C in Nino-3, and +3.9°C in Nino-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Nino.

The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Nino will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . Chances remain high for a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Nino events dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ): the chance is 54% for September-November, 83% for October-December, and 70% for November-January. With an event of this magnitude, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Nino are larger, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
